name: Suitable Replacement
description: You are given two strings s and t consisting of small Latin letters, string s can also contain '?' characters. Suitability of string s is calculated by following metric: Any two letters can be swapped positions, these operations can be performed arbitrary number of times over any pair of positions. Among all resulting strings s , you choose the one with the largest number of non-intersecting occurrences of string t . Suitability is this number of occurrences. You should replace all '?' characters with small Latin letters in such a way that the suitability of string s is maximal.
input_specification: The first line contains string s ( 1 ≤ | s | ≤ 10 6 ). The second line contains string t ( 1 ≤ | t | ≤ 10 6 ).
output_specification: Print string s with '?' replaced with small Latin letters in such a way that suitability of that string is maximal. If there are multiple strings with maximal suitability then print any of them.
approach_summary: Verify predicate monotonicity: P(x) is true for x ≤ K and false otherwise. Binary search over the answer domain to find the boundary in O(log(Range) × Verify_Time).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 825D — Suitable Replacement [33. Binary Search]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary search on the monotonic answer domain.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The predicate function $P(x)$ ('Is answer $\le x$ feasible?') is monotonic: if $P(x)$ is true for some value, it remains true for all larger values (or vice versa). This allows binary division of the answer search space $[\text{low}, \text{high}]$ in $O(\log(\text{Range}))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N \log(\text{Range}))$
  The binary search divides the search interval by 2 at each iteration, requiring $\log_2(\text{Range})$ steps. In each step, the feasibility check `check(mid)` scans the array in $\mathcal{O}(N)$ time.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(1)$ auxiliary space
  The algorithm operates directly over the input array without allocating extra auxiliary memory.
